edges.effect_quant: A 2020 Cochrane review of 12 studies with 1,473 randomized participants found uncertainty about whether probiotics reduced ulcerative-colitis relapse versus placebo (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.63-1.18) or improved remission maintenance versus placebo (RR 1.16, 95% CI 0.98-1.37); in a 2023 open-label LGG monotherapy study, 32 of 76 patients (42%) improved and 37% entered remission over one month.
edges.population: adults with ulcerative colitis in remission-maintenance or mild-to-moderate active disease studies that included Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG or broader probiotic comparators
edges.mechanism: Lactobacillus rhamnosus strains may influence ulcerative colitis activity by reinforcing epithelial barrier function, competing with pathobionts, and shaping mucosal cytokine signaling, but the clinical expression of those effects appears highly formulation- and context-dependent.
edges.summary: The clinical signal for Lactobacillus rhamnosus in ulcerative colitis is promising enough to stay on the table, but not clean enough to call established. Reviews of the broader probiotic literature remain uncertain, while a recent LGG monotherapy study suggests that some patients with mild-to-moderate disease can improve or even remit over short follow-up.
edges.caveats: Most remission-maintenance data are from heterogeneous probiotic formulations rather than head-to-head, adequately powered LGG trials. Open-label induction data are vulnerable to regression to the mean, spontaneous fluctuation, and concomitant-care effects even when mesalamine washout is attempted.
